To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the latency-associated nuclear antigen LANA supports latent DNA replication of KSHV in dividing cells and that the origin of DNA replication of Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpes virus is located within the terminal repeat.

(i) KSHV LANA is a DNA-binding protein that supports latent DNA replication of ori-containing plasmids in dividing cells and that (ii) LANA is a functional homologue to the ori-binding protein EBNA-1 of EBV.
LANA is required and sufficient for replication of KSHV DNA in transient replication assays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cis- and trans-acting factors involved in DNA replication and segregation of the KSHv genome.
the molecular mechanisms that are involved in the establishment and maintenance of the KSHv genome during the latent state.
the identification of the origin and the cis elements required for replication and segregation of the KSHv genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LANA, like EBNA1, supports replication of oriP plasmids in dividing cells.
LANA is required not only for genome segregation but also for DNA replication, thereby supporting the notion that LANA is an essential protein for the life cycle of KSHV.
LANA, like EBNA 1, is a multifunction protein with a variety of functions, including DNA replication, DNA segregation and gene silencing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LANA is not only a transcriptional regulator, but also a key protein that is involved in the regulation of viral DNA metabolism.
the KSHV genome is a unique structure in the gammaherpesvirus family, and LANA, a multifunctional viral protein, is the major player in the viral life cycle.
KSHV LANA is a multifunction protein that is involved in DNA replication, segregation, and transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KSHV genome, like that of Epstein-Barr virus, is replicated by a mechanism that is different from that of lytic DNA replication.
